## Analysis at each round
### Round 1
There are no trials yet in this search. The starting net scored 0 on both seeds. Across past searches, only one family ever scored above 0. It feeds the legal-action mask in as input channels under four layouts (as given, transposed, y-flipped, x-flipped), plus coordinate channels, and it sums per-type output maps re-laid in those same layouts. Recipe-only changes and other heads or trunks always scored 0. So round 1 has three candidates. The first rebuilds that family at about the starting net's compute (r≤1), to check whether this world rewards it. The second widens the hedge to all 8 dihedral layouts, in case this world's action indexing is rotated. The third keeps the four layouts and uses 2 PPO epochs, which gives about 1.86x more samples. Seeds can succeed or fail by luck. Nonzero late training success is the first real signal.

### Round 2
Every trial scored exactly 0 on both seeds and had 0 late training success. That includes the 4-layout and 8-dihedral mask family and the 2-epoch recipe. The family worked in an earlier world, so the likely problem is a mismatch between how this world numbers its actions and the [type, Y, X] layout these nets assume. All 8 flips and transposes of that layout are already ruled out. Two plausible orderings are left: cell-major order (action = cell*T + type) and an index offset (DONE first, so placements start at index 1). This round keeps the family's trunk and generalises the layout hedge to precomputed index permutations: P1 adds cell-major order, P2 adds the offset, and P3 combines both, so the results show which deviation matters. Any nonzero training success is the first real signal. If all three stay at 0, the deviation is not in the action indexing, and the next round should look at the dynamics or reward.

### Round 3
All six trials are effectively zero. The best, r2c2, scored 0.002: 2 of 512 dev designs on one seed. Training success was at most 0.0004, so there is no clear signal yet. Hedges over 8 dihedral layouts, type-major or cell-major order, and DONE first or last all failed. A 1x1 stem should learn any reordering of observation channels, and mixed layouts are already covered, so one of two things is likely true. Either the indexing deviation is DONE-first and the 32-layout hedge hid it, or this 8x8x6 world with up to 16 bricks is too hard to learn at this budget. The second calls for a better learning signal, not more layout guessing. This round runs three variants of r2c2 to separate these explanations: one cleaner DONE-first test, footprint-aware pooling for the landing layer, and more frequent PPO updates.

### Round 4
Every trial so far scored about 0. The mask-layout family that reached 0.22 in an earlier world almost fails to learn here: late training success is at most 0.0004. Spreading the layouts over cell-major order, all 8 dihedral layouts or a DONE-first offset has not lifted it. The best result, r2c2 at 0.002, is two exact builds on one seed, which is within noise. Since no index layout we tried stands out, the problem may be learning difficulty rather than an indexing mismatch. That fits a larger 8x8x6 world, where exact builds need wider spatial reasoning. In this last round I keep r2c2 as the base and make one change per candidate. (1) Use the unused compute on a deeper residual trunk, which widens the receptive field to 7 cells at the same step budget. (2) Add a zero-initialised dense head from global features to every action index, in case DONE or some actions sit at an index the layouts don't cover. (3) A recipe aimed at precise behaviour: lower entropy and longer credit assignment.

## Trial it ended with
name: Dihedral layouts with DONE-first offset
hypothesis: This world may put DONE at index 0 and shift every placement by one, which the earlier layout hedges cannot catch. This net covers both offsets (DONE last, and DONE first with placements shifted), each over 8 type-major dihedral layouts, with one DONE head per offset. If it learns where the plain 8-layout net scored 0, the indices are shifted. If both seeds score 0, an offset is not the deviation.
